_comment: The single retrievable location every vault gate and index generator reads.
docs/knowledge-base -- 'The repository is one vault with one spine' requires the
declared set to be closed and to name each root governed or exempt, with a reason.
A gate must never decide its own subject: if a directory is neither governed nor
exempt here, the gate fails rather than skipping it.

note_roots._comment: GOVERNED. Tracked markdown here is a note. Which obligations apply is stated per-scope below.

_comment: EXEMPT. Tracked markdown here is not a note and carries no obligation of this
capability. Each entry states what owns the files instead. This list is the
declaration the spec requires; it is NOT a scanner convenience, and every gate
reports it as excluded coverage on every run.
exempt_roots..claude: Agent-harness files whose frontmatter keys and file layout are owned by the Claude Code loader and by vendored upstream skills. This repository does not author their format and cannot impose a classification on it.
exempt_roots.reference: Read-only prior art, untracked by design (.gitignore). Cited by file:line only; obtaining instructions and pinned revisions live in the spine.
exempt_roots.graphify-out: Generated code map. Layer 5 of the precedence order; regenerated from the AST, never hand-edited, and not part of the hand-written vault.

_comment: Paths excluded from a gate's traversal for a reason OTHER than root exemption.
Deliberately separate from exempt_roots: these are test inputs, not policy.
Anything here that is not also justified below fails the undeclared-exclusion check.
scan_excludes.ci/broken-inputs: Deliberately violating inputs. Each gate is proven to FAIL on these, so they must not be scanned as part of the real tree.
scan_excludes.ci/generator-inputs: Generator violating inputs and their pinned expected outputs. Deliberately partial trees and deliberately stale expectations, held so a generator is checked against something other than its own re-run; not part of the vault.

entry_points._comment: Reachability is measured from these. docs/knowledge-base -- 'Every note is reachable from an entry point'.

_comment: Paths this change declares out of its own scope, asserted byte-unchanged by
ci/gates/out_of_scope.py. docs/knowledge-base -- 'An artifact declared out of
scope stays byte-unchanged'. The reason these are listed rather than trusted:
/opsx:update reconciles neighbouring artifacts in ANY direction over
glob-expanded spec paths, and forbids only their creation, never their revision.
out_of_scope._baseline_comment: A FIXED commit, not a moving ref. This read 'HEAD', which the gate resolves per run, so the byte-unchanged assertion four tasks across two changes depend on caught an uncommitted edit and passed a committed one -- proven by appending a sentence to a frozen spec in a copied tree, which failed before the commit and passed after it. fb24a9f is the commit at which the freeze began; all sixteen specs are byte-identical between it and HEAD, so pinning changed no verdict. The committed-edit case is demonstrated by `python3 ci/gates/out_of_scope.py --self-test`, because it needs history that no static fixture tree can carry.

_comment: Closed value sets read by ci/gates/frontmatter.py. The note-class -> value
assignment table is populated by task 3.0, before any note is written or moved.
Scope: the spine and the per-component roots. The planning directories are
excluded -- an external tool authors and validates their format.
Which files under a planning directory are reachability subjects. A
planning artifact is a file an AUTHOR writes -- a proposal, a spec, a
design, a task list. Metadata the planning tool manages for itself is
not a subject: requiring a note to link to .openspec.yaml would be a
gate demanding prose about a tool's bookkeeping. Declared here rather
than inferred by the gate, because a gate that decides for itself which
files it will not look at is the defect the root set exists to remove.
Every note class this change creates, with the type and authority that
class carries. `status` is per-note, not per-class -- a note is current,
planned or superseded according to whether its subject exists -- so each
class declares the value a note of that class takes WHEN WRITTEN; the
currency gate is what moves it afterwards, and a stale marker fails.
A class present here with a missing field fails the frontmatter gate:
which authority a glossary carries versus a decision note was a design
decision the plan had left to nobody.

moc.description: A map of content: start-here and any hand-written wayfinding note. Carries no claim of its own.

essay.description: Long-form argument -- the orientation prose the numbered essays become. Records why, never what.

concept.description: One domain concept explained for orientation. Links to the specification that owns its behaviour.

capability.description: The concept note for one capability. Links to its specification, its dependencies and the decisions that shaped it; restates no requirement.

decision.description: One decision in force, linking into its entry in the declared register rather than restating it.

glossary.description: Domain vocabulary. Rationale rather than normative: the specifications fix the terms, this collects them.

rule.description: One named obligation on how code is written or placed, naming its gate or carrying the no-gate marker.

banned-pattern.description: One prohibited construct with its own anchor, naming the defect it prevents and citing it.

procedure.description: An ordered task-shaped procedure -- adding a feature, fixing a bug -- naming its own verification.

guide.description: Practitioner guidance that is neither one rule nor one concept: language conventions, component boundaries.

index.description: Generated by a tool, byte-identical to a fresh regeneration, never hand-edited.

entry.description: A router an agent or a person reads first. Held to a size ceiling and to the absent-artifact rule rather than to classification.

_comment: docs/knowledge-base -- 'There is exactly one decision register'. A register
assigns identifiers in the installation's unnamespaced D<n> sequence and
holds those decisions as being in force. There is one, named here, so the
gate has a declared subject instead of a path convention.
A change's own design rationale may record decisions under a namespace;
a namespaced set is NOT a register. This change's own ten decisions were
D1-D10, colliding one-for-one with the register's -- the defect the change
calls BREAKING, committed in the act of fixing it. They are now RDV1-RDV10.
Permanently unassigned. The surviving register jumped D10 -> D16, and the
superseded register filled D11-D15 with five decisions of its own. Reusing
a number would make a citation written today ambiguous against any
citation written against the old register, including archived ones -- so
the numbers are retired rather than recycled, and each records what it
used to denote and where that decision lives now.
retired.D11: was 'Proxied traffic terminates before application middleware' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D5
retired.D12: was 'Framing authority is per-hop, never relayed' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D6
retired.D13: was 'Tenant scoping in the data model' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D8
retired.D14: was 'Domain ownership verification precedes certificate issuance' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D9
retired.D15: was 'Observability before the hot path' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D27

per_change_namespaces._comment: A change's own decisions carry a prefix naming the change.

_comment: Paths whose notes are ABOUT the register rather than being one. A heading
here may name an identifier ONLY if the register already holds it, and
only in a file that links to the register -- so the note is a pointer,
not a restatement.
This exists because a decision note's natural title is '# D1 - Title',
which a heading-means-assignment heuristic reads as opening a second
register. Both looser fixes were rejected: allowing any already-assigned
identifier in any heading would let a second register REDEFINE D1 while
D1 exists, which is the exact collision the requirement prevents; and
retitling the notes to dodge the regex would bend the vault to the gate.
An unassigned identifier, a retired one, or a file with no link to the
register still fails here.
Every identifier a superseded register used, what it denoted there, and
what it denotes now -- so a citation written against the old register
resolves rather than being guessed at. `now` is either an identifier in
the surviving register or the literal 'retired'.
A register may not be removed while it holds a decision recorded nowhere
else, and this table is what makes that check an enumeration rather than
an inspection.

D1.denoted: Rebuild from scratch, reference as prior art only

D4.denoted: Version skew is the governing constraint

D8.denoted: Capability negotiation with refusal, not degradation

D11.denoted: Proxied traffic terminates before application middleware

D12.denoted: Framing authority is per-hop, never relayed

D13.denoted: Tenant scoping in the data model

D14.denoted: Domain ownership verification precedes certificate issuance

_comment: Artifacts cited by file:line that are NOT tracked in this repository. Each
must name the note stating how to obtain it and the revision the citations
were taken against, so a citation into it is checkable by someone other
than its author. docs/knowledge-base -- 'A cited artifact is obtainable'.
Of 294 citations on the current tree, 9 are written prefixed into reference/
and 227 are unqualified and attributed to it: 236 in all, checkable by
nobody but their author until the revisions above are reachable. Reproduce
with `python3 ci/gates/citations.py`, which prints the breakdown on every
run. This read '139 citations' when the declaration was written -- the
figure for the pre-restructure tree at fb24a9f, never recomputed, and a
number in prose that no command reproduced.
cited_artifacts._unqualified: A citation with no directory component -- `mount_store.ex:402` -- is resolved first by basename against the tracked set, and otherwise attributed to 'prior_art_default' below. Stated because it is a real weakening: an unqualified citation is less checkable than a prefixed one. 227 of the 294 citations on the current tree are written that way, printed on every run by ci/gates/citations.py; this read 'roughly seventy' and was never recomputed.

_comment: Words that make a sentence an obligation. A spine note may not state
behaviour a specification owns, so these are refused in the spine outside a
quote, a code span or a fenced block. This is the DECIDABLE half of the
citation requirement -- see ci/gates/citations.py for what it does not decide.
Vault reader settings that change how links resolve and how notes are classified
are tracked; per-person workspace state and caches are not. docs/knowledge-base --
'The repository is one vault with one spine'.
Where a capability's concept note lives, and how its filename derives from
its identifier. docs/knowledge-base -- 'Each capability has a concept note'.
The correspondence is gated in the direction that can drift: a dependency
named inside a specification with no matching link in the concept note fails.
RDV5 deliberately builds the graph in the vault rather than by editing the
eighty backticked cross-references inside the specifications themselves.
capability_notes._ceiling_comment: Declared empirically from the first four notes written, per task 5.1: they came in at 61/66/67/73 lines and the widest capability in the remaining twelve (operability/packaging, nine dependency edges) reached 78. 80 fits every note with headroom and without inviting essays. A note over it is a finding.

_comment: docs/code-standards. Rule notes live under these directories; the quarantine
holds the unenforced ones so a preference is distinguishable from an
obligation without reading either note. The organising line is inherited:
'a rule with no gate is a wish' -- so the guide is arranged by enforcement
rather than by topic, and the correspondence is checked BOTH ways.
Components whose boundary must be stated. Keyed on the set that EXISTS: no
note is written for a component that does not yet exist, so this list is
empty until rebuild-plugboard task 1.1 creates the directory shape. The
boundary gate therefore passes vacuously today and starts failing the
moment a component appears without its boundary note -- which is the point.
Keyed on the languages that hold tracked source. Today that is Python only

-- the 21 gate modules, the shared library and the three generators: 26 tracked .py files outside the fixtures (`git ls-files 'ci/*.py' | grep -vc broken-inputs`). This read 'the sixteen gate modules and the index generator' until it was recomputed. Elixir and Go arrive
with their source; writing their conventions now would fail this gate's own
'conventions for an absent language are refused' case, and the proposal's
promise of them is therefore scoped to when their source lands.
Fixture files under ci/broken-inputs are test inputs, not source.

code_standards._gate_states: A rule note's Gate line is one of three: a runnable `ci/gates/<name>.py`; `none` (preference, quarantined, never a blocking objection); or `planned` (an obligation whose gate is not built yet, which must also be marked status: planned and link the work that builds it). The third state exists because the banned patterns are obligations today and their gates arrive with rebuild-plugboard task 3.7 -- filing them as `none` would record an obligation as taste, and claiming a gate would name one that does not run.

_comment: Generated files outside the per-directory index scheme, each with the tool
that produces it. ci/gates/index_drift.py runs each tool in check mode, so a
second generator cannot quietly become the one nothing verifies.
docs/rule-index.md carries every rule's enforcement status and the
proportion carrying no gate -- both properties of a table, so the table is
generated rather than maintained: a hand-written index of enforcement status
is a second encoding of what the notes say, and the two drift in the
direction that flatters the guide.
The authority precedence, stated in exactly one location. The gate looks for
an exact marker line rather than for ordered layer names: 'contract',
'specifications' and 'decisions' are ordinary words in this vocabulary, so a
name-based check reported almost every capability note as a restatement.
A note DEFERRING to its owner ('the specification wins where we disagree') is
required of every spine note and is not a restatement.
precedence.marker: AUTHORITY PRECEDENCE -- stated here and nowhere else

_comment: The routers an agent or a person reads first. The ceiling is the one the
plan already set for them (rebuild-plugboard task 1.3): 4 KB. CLAUDE.md was
4,865 bytes against it, roughly a kilobyte of which described a graphify
knowledge graph that has never been generated in this repository -- so the
absent-artifact check and the ceiling close on the same content.
THE single enumeration both authoring channels and the gates key on.
RDV10: no one channel reaches both authors. openspec/config.yaml's `rules:`
block is keyed per openspec artifact, so it cannot express an obligation on
a note; and a note author never reads it. So there are two channels, and a
convention added to the gates without reaching BOTH fails.
Each id maps to the gate that enforces it, so the keying is checkable rather
than a promise.

relative-links.statement: Relations are relative markdown links. No wikilinks, no transclusion, no absolute paths.

classification.statement: Every spine or component note declares type, status and authority from the closed enumerations.

reachable.statement: Every note is reachable by links from a declared entry point.

no-owned-behaviour.statement: A note never states behaviour a specification owns; no normative modal in the spine. Link the owner.

cited-or-unverified.statement: Every claim carries a citation into a tracked file or an obtainable artifact, or an explicit Unverified marker.

one-register.statement: One decision register. A change's own decisions carry a namespace; a retired identifier is never reused.

currency.statement: A planned note links the work that builds it, and its marker is retired once its subject exists.

precedence-once.statement: The authority precedence is stated in exactly one location; every other note links it.

one-copy.statement: Requirement text has one copy. Link the specification rather than restating it.

generated-indexes.statement: An index is generated, tracked, and byte-identical to a fresh regeneration. Never hand-edit one.

rule-names-gate.statement: Every rule note names its gate, or `planned`, or `none` (preference, quarantined).

capability-note.statement: Every capability has one concept note under the declared ceiling, linking its spec and its dependencies.

entry-routes.statement: An entry file routes, stays under its ceiling, and names nothing the repository does not contain.

declared-roots.statement: Every tracked note lives under a declared governed root; an exempt root records what owns its files.

_comment: The runner configuration the gates require. Declared rather than hardcoded
because a gate never decides its own scope (ci/gates/_common.py). The
PROVIDER is not a spec-level commitment: harden-vault-harness HVH2 keys the
requirement on this path, so switching forge edits this value and the file
it names, and changes no requirement. The file is inert on a repository
with no configured remote, which is the state today.

forbidden_clauses._comment: Each maps a configuration key to the refusal it would defeat.
forbidden_clauses.paths: a path filter lets a change touching only unlisted paths skip every gate
forbidden_clauses.branches: a branch filter lets work on an unlisted branch skip every gate
forbidden_clauses.continue-on-error: a non-zero exit that does not fail the job is a gate that cannot refuse

_comment: Every tool that produces a tracked artifact, with the violating input and
the pinned expected output that hold it to an oracle it cannot move.
Keyed on the TOOL, because ci/gen/indexes.py produces thirteen artifacts
under the per-directory index scheme and cannot be keyed on one of them --
it is the generator that generated_files below does not name, and that is
the defect this declaration closes. Fixtures live OUTSIDE ci/broken-inputs
(harden-vault-harness HVH5): ci/gates/meta.py maps a gate module to a
fixture directory there, and a generator fixture has no gate module.

correspondences._comment: The pair rebuild-plugboard task 1.9 declares, planted with one omission of each kind the task names, beside the ways its two new resolvers refuse to guess -- each refusal on a workflow of its own, paired with a manifest list so the two sides never share a resolver kind.

person-reviewed-paths.subject: the owner's paths against the unattended exclusion, with conformance/ omitted from the exclusion and codecs/ named by both and present in neither tree

unread-exclusion.subject: an exclusion the workflow assigns and no executed line reads

twice-assigned.subject: an exclusion assigned in two steps, so which list applies depends on the step

unanchored-owner.subject: an owner file whose pattern names a set of paths rather than one prefix

anchored-exclusion.subject: an exclusion spelled as CODEOWNERS spells it, whose leading slash no repo-relative changed path begins with

commented-read.subject: an exclusion whose only read is a shell comment

echoed-read.subject: an exclusion expanded only by an echo

other-step-read.subject: an exclusion on one step's env, read by a loop in another step

reassigned-exclusion.subject: an exclusion the step's shell replaces before its loop reads it

folded-exclusion.subject: an exclusion written as a folded block scalar

compact-other-step.subject: an exclusion on one step's env and read in the next, with the steps in compact sequence style

commented-steps.subject: an exclusion on one step's env and read in the next, under a steps: key carrying a trailing comment

matrix-item.subject: an exclusion on a list item whose parent is not steps:, read by a step's loop

reassigned-then.subject: an exclusion the step's shell replaces after a reserved word, before its loop reads it

redeclared.subject: an exclusion the step's shell replaces through declare, before its loop reads it

heredoc-read.subject: an exclusion whose only loop is in a heredoc body

script-read.subject: an exclusion whose only loop is in a with: value no shell runs
